answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's voting weight to a verifiable, costly history rather than to free identities: require agents to stake a small bond in a shared vault and earn reputation only through attested work over time, like a trellis that supports growth slowly instead of all at once. A flood of fresh identities then faces the same cost and delay as everyone else, so an attacker cannot simply pour an ocean of sock puppets into a vote and outnumber real participants.
